overview: Anhui Conch Cement is one of China's largest integrated cement producers, manufacturing and selling cement, clinker, aggregates and commodity concrete from its base in Anhui Province, with over 600 marketing departments across China and a growing overseas footprint (Indonesia, Cambodia, and other Asian/African markets). The Group is vertically diversifying downstream into aggregates, ready-mix concrete, dry-mix mortar/ceramic tile glue and other consumption building materials to offset structural decline in core domestic cement demand, while also building out new-energy (wind/solar/storage) and environmental-protection businesses alongside its listed affiliates (Conch Venture 0586.HK, Conch Environment Protection 0587.HK, Conch Material Technology 2560.HK). It reports in RMB under a December fiscal year end and is dual-listed as A shares (600585.SH) and H shares (0914.HK).

business_model.summary: Conch makes money primarily from selling self-produced cement and clinker (32.5/42.5/52.5-grade) to infrastructure and real-estate construction markets via a direct-sales-led, distribution-supplemented regional network; it is a capital-intensive, scale/cost-leadership commodity business whose margins are a direct function of coal/power input costs versus a cement selling price that is set regionally and highly cyclical. In response to China's structural cement overcapacity and falling demand, Conch has been extending its industrial chain downstream into aggregates and commodity concrete (higher/more stable margins than cement) and into consumer-facing building materials (mortar, tile glue, putty), while also growing overseas cement/clinker sales (Cambodia, Indonesia) where pricing and demand have been more resilient.
business_model.customer_type: B2B - infrastructure contractors, property developers, distributors, and government-linked construction projects (railways, highways, airports, water conservancy, urban renewal)
business_model.geographic_mix: East China ~27%, Central China ~27%, South China ~18%, West China ~18%, Export ~1%, Overseas (Cambodia, Indonesia and other projects) ~4-9% and growing; overseas assets were 7.3% of total assets as of H1 2026

main_competitors: Huaxin Building Materials Group (formerly Huaxin Cement, 600801.SH/6655.HK)
West China Cement (2233.HK, a Conch associate)
competitive_position.market_position: One of China's two largest cement groups by production capacity and sales volume (alongside state-backed CNBM), with clinker/cement/aggregate/concrete capacity of 234 million / 385 million / 186 million tonnes and 84.35 million m3 respectively as of H1 2026; widely regarded as the lowest-cost, highest-efficiency major producer in the industry (the 'Conch Model')

moat_factors.description: Decades of lean operations, large-scale dry-process kilns, captive limestone quarries, scale procurement, and continuous efficiency investment (AI-driven process control, alternative fuels) give Conch among the lowest unit costs in the industry (~RMB163-166/tonne in 2025/H1 2026)
Long-term control of limestone quarries near plants reduces raw material cost and supports expansion into aggregates using the same resource base

Extensive clinker/cement capacity concentrated along the Yangtze River and coastal waterways, supported by 600+ marketing departments and waterway logistics, gives distribution cost and market-density advantages

Low gearing (~20% PRC-basis, net gearing ~7-9%) and a large net cash position give Conch capacity to acquire distressed competitor assets and fund counter-cyclical capex/buybacks that smaller, more leveraged peers cannot match

Strong brand recognition domestically and a track record of executing large-scale capacity-replacement and overseas projects positions it to benefit from government-led industry consolidation ('anti-involution') policy

weaknesses: Still overwhelmingly dependent (>85% of revenue) on core domestic cement/clinker, a commodity product in structural demand decline
Limited pricing power given cement is a low-differentiation, transport-cost-limited regional commodity; price is largely set by local supply-demand balance, not by Conch
Aggregates/concrete/new-materials diversification remains a small (and in some periods margin-compressed) share of revenue, not yet large enough to offset cement declines
Overseas business, while growing, is still a small fraction (~7-9%) of assets/revenue, limiting its ability to fully offset domestic weakness
Exposure to coal and power cost volatility which can move faster than cement selling prices can adjust

growth_drivers: Industrial chain extension into aggregates, commodity concrete, dry-mix mortar, ceramic tile glue and putty powder to build a 'one-stop' comprehensive building materials offering

Overseas capacity expansion - Phnom Penh Conch (Cambodia) commenced operations in 2025; West Papua Conch (Indonesia, 51%-owned) continues to receive capital injections; broader strategy to pursue M&A in 'favorable domestic markets and untapped overseas markets'

Domestic industry consolidation ('anti-involution' policy) - government capacity-control measures (2025-2026 Work Plan for Stabilizing Growth in the Building Materials Industry) that prohibit new capacity and push misaligned actual-vs-registered capacity into retirement could, over time, improve supply-demand balance for the largest, lowest-cost survivor

Related-party consolidation - 2026 acquisition of Wanwei/Mengwei Technology cement assets (~RMB619m) as Conch Holdings exits cement production and sales businesses in favor of the listco, continuing a long-running pattern of capacity roll-up

New energy and environmental businesses (wind/solar/storage ~1.4GW installed, fly-ash disposal, construction-waste resource utilization) diversifying earnings and supporting decarbonization of the core business
AI and digital/intelligent manufacturing (building materials industry's first AI large-model deployment across 40+ production scenarios) to structurally lower costs further

Capital return - active share buyback program (RMB600m-1,000m approved May 2026) and consistent dividend payout (RMB0.85/share for FY2025) signal management's confidence and shareholder-friendly capital allocation amid depressed valuation

business.description: Cement demand is highly correlated with fixed-asset investment and real estate development investment, both of which turned negative/continued declining in 2025-2026; national cement output fell 6.9% in 2025 and a further 8% in H1 2026

Industry capacity utilization fell below 50% in late 2025; overcapacity of roughly 30% is expected to persist even after capacity-replacement measures, intensifying price competition and compressing margins industry-wide

Aggregates and commodity concrete margins have themselves been compressing (aggregates gross margin down 3-7 points in recent periods), showing diversification is not immune to the same demand/pricing pressures as cement

Repeated connected-party acquisitions of cement assets from Conch Holdings/Wanwei Group affiliates raise governance questions around pricing and minority shareholder treatment, though historically modest in scale

financial.description: RMB appreciation versus other currencies drove a swing in financial expenses (net exchange losses) in H1 2026, and overseas USD-denominated subsidiary investments (Conch HK, West Papua Conch) carry currency translation risk

Cash at bank fell sharply (down ~32% H1 2026) as funds were redeployed into wealth management products, structured deposits and income notes - a conservative yield strategy but one that introduces some counterparty/liquidity risk relative to holding cash

regulatory.description: Cement industry's inclusion in China's national carbon emissions trading market, and ongoing 'dual carbon' / ultra-low-emission mandates, are expected to raise production and compliance costs over time

'Anti-involution' capacity-control and off-peak production mandates could help large players like Conch longer-term, but near-term compliance and capacity-alignment requirements add cost and operational complexity

macro.description: Fuel and power costs are by far the largest input (52-57% of unit cost); coal price swings materially affect margins faster than cement prices typically adjust, as seen in H1 2026 when energy costs rose while selling prices fell

macro.risk: China macro slowdown / fiscal stimulus dependency
macro.description: Cement demand is highly levered to government infrastructure stimulus (special bond issuance, major national strategy projects); any pullback in fiscal support or slower-than-expected urban renewal programs would directly hit volumes

macro_factors.industry_outlook: China's cement industry remains in a multi-year structural downcycle; national cement output fell 6.9% in 2025 to 1.693 billion tonnes and a further ~8% in H1 2026, with most forecasters (e.g., SunSirs) projecting another ~5% decline in 2026 to around 1.6 billion tonnes and persistent ~30% overcapacity even after government-mandated capacity rationalization
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - cement is a late-cycle, construction/infrastructure-linked commodity with earnings that swing sharply with property and fixed-asset investment cycles, as shown by H1 2026 net profit falling 42.8% on a 10.9% revenue decline
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate indirect sensitivity - lower rates support property/infrastructure investment (a long-term demand driver) and reduce financing costs for developers/contractors who are Conch's end customers; direct balance sheet sensitivity is low given Conch's net cash position and low gearing (~20%)
key_input_costs: Limestone and other raw materials (largely self-sourced)

recent_developments.event: Revenue fell 10.9% YoY to RMB36.9bn and net profit attributable to shareholders fell 42.8% YoY to RMB2.53bn, driven by sharply lower domestic cement selling prices amid intensifying competition, partly offset by cost control and strong overseas growth (overseas revenue +21%, margin +2.2pp; export revenue +77%)

Group completed 4 new aggregates projects, 26 new commodity concrete projects (construction, leasing, toll processing) and 4 new dry-mix mortar/ceramic tile glue projects, continuing industrial-chain extension
Board approved a share buyback program of RMB600m-1,000m (price cap RMB27.71/share); as of end-July 2026 the company had repurchased ~21.5 million A shares (~0.41% of share capital) for ~RMB382.7m

Subsidiaries agreed to acquire cement production assets (Chaohu and Wulanchabu facilities) from Wanwei Group/Mengwei Technology for a combined consideration of roughly RMB619-691 million, as parent Conch Holdings exits direct cement production/sales in favor of the listed company - part of ongoing group-level consolidation of cement assets into Conch Cement
FY2025 final dividend of RMB0.61/share paid (together with the RMB0.24/share 2025 interim dividend, totaling RMB0.85/share for the year), alongside an interim 2026 dividend proposal of RMB0.13/share

FY2025 revenue fell 9.3% YoY to RMB82.5bn but net profit attributable to shareholders rose 5.4% YoY to RMB8.1bn (PRC basis) as cost reductions (fuel/power costs down ~15.7% per tonne) more than offset lower selling prices and sales volumes

Phnom Penh Conch (Cambodia) plant successfully completed and commenced operations, adding to the Group's overseas platform; continued capital injections into West Papua Conch (Indonesia, 51%-owned JV) and the Yili/Xinjiang Yaobai cement asset acquisition completed in the domestic market

Six PRC ministries (led by MIIT) issued the Work Plan for Stabilizing Growth in the Building Materials Industry (2025-2026), prohibiting new cement/clinker capacity additions and pushing alignment of actual vs. registered capacity - a policy tailwind for large compliant incumbents like Conch over time

items.metric: Self-produced cement and clinker sales volume
items.notes: Down from 265 million tonnes actually sold in FY2025, reflecting management's expectation of continued demand softness; management stated this is not a binding commitment to investors

items.metric: Unit cost and unit expense per tonne
items.notes: Management expects to hold per-tonne cost/expense roughly flat via continued cost-control measures, alternative fuel usage and procurement optimization

Up modestly from RMB11,032 million actually spent in FY2025; to be financed mainly by internal resources, directed at core-business project development, industrial-chain extension, energy-conservation retrofits, and new productive forces
A-share buyback at a price cap of RMB27.71/share; ~RMB382.7m executed by end-July 2026

guidance.management_commentary: Management's 2026 outlook flags three principal risks it will actively manage: (1) demand fluctuation risk tied to fixed-asset and real estate investment trends, (2) risk of intensified low-price competition amid persistent overcapacity (responded to via support for 'anti-involution' industry self-regulation and capacity reduction), and (3) rising environmental/carbon compliance costs from 'dual carbon' policy and inclusion in the national carbon trading market. Management describes 2026 as the first year of the 15th Five-Year Plan, expecting accelerated infrastructure investment and urban renewal to partially offset real estate weakness, while continuing to pursue domestic and overseas M&A, industrial-chain extension (aggregates/concrete/consumer building materials), and new-energy/environmental business growth.

bull_case: Lowest-cost, largest-scale producer with a fortress balance sheet (net cash, ~20% gearing) positions Conch to gain share and acquire distressed competitor capacity as the industry consolidates under government-mandated capacity controls

Active share buybacks (RMB600m-1bn in 2026) and a consistent, substantial dividend (RMB0.85/share FY2025, implying a high yield at depressed share prices) signal shareholder-friendly capital return even in a cyclical trough

Overseas expansion (Cambodia operational, Indonesia/West Papua JV, export growth of 77% YoY in H1 2026) is delivering simultaneous volume and price growth, providing a structural offset to domestic cement weakness

Industrial-chain diversification into aggregates, commodity concrete and consumer building materials, plus new-energy and environmental businesses, gradually reduces pure-play cement cyclicality over time

Analyst sentiment is notably positive (consensus 'Strong Buy' per Investing.com, average 12-month target materially above recent trading levels), reflecting a view that China cement is near a cyclical trough with policy-driven consolidation ahead
bear_case: China's structural property/construction downturn shows no clear bottom - national cement demand fell 6.9% in 2025 and ~8% further in H1 2026, with H1 2026 net profit down 42.8% YoY, showing earnings remain highly exposed to a demand cycle still in decline

Persistent industry overcapacity (utilization below 50%, ~30% structural overcapacity even post-rationalization per third-party forecasts) means pricing power is likely to stay weak for an extended period regardless of Conch's own cost advantages

Diversification into aggregates/concrete has not been margin-immune - gross margins in these newer segments have themselves compressed in recent periods, raising questions about how much they can really offset core cement declines
Overseas and new-energy/environmental growth remains a small fraction of the overall business (~7-9% of assets), unlikely to materially offset domestic revenue declines in the near-to-medium term

Carbon/environmental compliance costs are set to rise structurally (national ETS inclusion, dual-carbon mandates), adding a cost headwind on top of already-thin cement margins at a time when pricing power is constrained
